caveats: Do not attempt to fit a model with both batch and condition as covariates — the design matrix will be singular/aliased since batch perfectly predicts condition
PCA separation by PC1 should not be interpreted as evidence of a treatment effect on its own since it is equally consistent with a pure batch effect
steps.context: Input: /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 13, raw salmon gene counts, first column gene symbol) and /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 3: sample, condition, batch). Design is stated in the data context to be perfectly confounded: batch B1 = all 6 controls, batch B2 = all 6 treated.
steps.question: Do the lung RNA-seq samples separate by condition (treated vs control) and/or by batch (B1 vs B2), and is that separation identical for both grouping variables given that batch is perfectly confounded with condition in this 12-sample, 12000-gene dataset?
acceptance_criteria: Library size, total counts, and detected-gene-count QC metrics reported per sample from counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples)

PCA computed on variance-stabilized or log-CPM counts, with PC1/PC2 plot colored by condition and separately by batch, demonstrating the two colorings are identical (since B1=all controls, B2=all treated)

A written statement in step output that the design matrix (~condition) and (~batch) are aliased/collinear (rank-deficient jointly), so batch cannot be included as a DESeq2 covariate alongside condition
Output includes a per-sample metadata table confirming the confound pattern

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
caveats: Any downstream consumer of this gene list must be told the effect size/significance reflects treatment confounded with processing batch
log2FoldChange shrinkage (apeglm) recommended for reporting effect sizes given the small n (6 vs 6)
steps.context: Same counts.csv and metadata.csv as T1S1. This is the primary DE analysis requested by the research question, but the confound identified in T1S1 (batch B1=control, B2=treated) means the resulting gene list reflects the combined treatment+batch effect and cannot be decomposed further with this design.
steps.question: Using DESeq2 on the 12000-gene x 12-sample raw count matrix with the model ~condition (treated vs control), which genes are differentially expressed, understanding this result is fully confounded with batch B2 vs B1 and cannot isolate a treatment-specific effect?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~condition on raw integer counts, treated vs control contrast, using the standard Wald test and independent filtering
Output table of all genes with log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj), plus counts of genes at padj<0.05 and |log2FC|>1
MA plot and volcano plot produced

Explicit caveat text attached to the results object/output stating the DE list is confounded with batch and should be interpreted as 'treatment-or-batch' differences, not attributable to treatment alone
No batch term added to the DESeq2 design (would produce a rank-deficient/aliased model given the confound) — this is stated as a limitation, not worked around

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes (WikiPathways human)
caveats: This step characterizes what the DE signature is biologically about but cannot resolve whether that signature is driven by drug treatment or by the batch/processing difference, since the confound in T1S2's input persists downstream
steps.context: Reference needed: a human pathway gene set collection (WikiPathways) for HGNC gene symbols, matching the gene symbols used as row identifiers in counts.csv. A WikiPathways human GMT file is available in the environment's reference store, formatted with a '%'-delimited descriptor field to recover the pathway name and HGNC gene symbol members.
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among the treated-vs-control DE genes identified in T1S2, reported with the same confound caveat (enrichment may reflect batch/processing artifacts as much as treatment biology)?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment run using the human WikiPathways gene sets against the DE gene list (padj<0.05 genes as foreground, or full ranked list for GSEA) from T1S2
Output table of enriched pathways with adjusted p-values, and a note re-stating the batch-condition confound explicitly next to the results
If the WikiPathways human GMT reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports that gap explicitly rather than fabricating pathway results

plan.title: Confounded lung treatment vs control DE analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context is explicit: 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples, but batch B1 contains all controls and B2 contains all treated samples — batch is completely confounded with condition (design matrix is rank-deficient for separating the two). No statistical method, including DESeq2 with a batch term, ComBat, or SVA, can distinguish a condition effect from a batch effect here, because the two factors are perfectly collinear (every B1 sample is control, every B2 sample is treated). Any 'batch-corrected' DE result would be fabricating a separation between technical and biological signal that the design cannot support. The only defensible path is: (1) run standard DESeq2 differential expression treated vs control, generate full QC diagnostics (library size, PCA, dispersion) so any candidate batch-driven separation is visible, (2) explicitly quantify and report the confound (PCA on PC1 aligning perfectly with both condition and batch, since they are identical groupings), (3) report the DE gene list with an explicit, unambiguous caveat that these genes cannot be attributed to treatment versus batch/processing effects, (4) run pathway enrichment on the resulting DE list against WikiPathways human, again flagging that any enriched pathway is a candidate for either treatment biology or batch artifact and cannot be disambiguated from these data alone. This plan does not attempt to 'fix' the confound statistically (that is not possible), it makes the limitation explicit and quantified rather than hiding it in a normal-looking DE workflow.
